title: invariant on Types
concept: A type invariant is a condition that must hold for every value of that type, checked at creation and after every mutation.
why: Without invariants, you must scatter validation checks everywhere. With invariants, check once at construction, and the compiler guarantees validity forever.
tips: Use invariants for domain types: Email, PhoneNumber, PositiveInt, NonEmptyStr
Invariants eliminate defensive checks inside functions — check once, trust everywhere
Combine invariants with contracts: invariant guards the TYPE, requires/ensures guard the FUNCTION
Multiple invariants are checked independently — use simple, focused conditions
common_mistakes: Writing invariants that are too expensive to check (e.g., scanning a large vector every time)
Leaking unvalidated values into invariant types — always validate at construction
Circular invariants that can never be satisfied — test with a simple constructor first
